title: Delegation and Oversight of the Investment Manager
summary: How the board delegates portfolio management while retaining responsibility, and the oversight framework needed to hold the investment manager to account without making investment decisions itself.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How the board delegates portfolio management while retaining responsibility, and the oversight framework needed to hold the investment manager to account without making investment decisions itself.
Learning Objectives: Assess the due diligence and contractual terms underpinning delegation
Evaluate performance, risk and mandate compliance reporting from the investment manager
Challenge the manager while respecting the line between oversight and management
Syllabus: Delegation versus abdication: what the board cannot hand over
Initial and ongoing due diligence, mandates and investment restrictions
Performance, risk and breach reporting to the board
Fear of micromanaging: monitoring without directing investment decisions
Intended Audience: Independent and non-executive directors of investment funds and fund management companies
Executive directors, designated persons and conducting officers of fund management companies
Company secretaries, governance leads and service provider relationship managers supporting fund boards
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of investment funds or asset management is helpful. No prior board experience is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)
